steps.content: [Chapter One: An Ordinary Family]

This is a perfectly ordinary Eastside family. The father drives freight for a living. The mother works the counter at a convenience store. The living room walls are covered in old, ordinary stickers. Beneath the glass of the coffee table, an ordinary family photo sits pressed flat.

The only thing that does not fit is the daughter, who is anything but ordinary.
Brilliance from humble roots, they call it. Her grades are exceptional. Her mind simply works differently.

The extraordinary daughter accepts the tutoring schedule her ordinary mother has scraped together every penny to afford. She holds the secondhand textbooks, marked by her ordinary father's fingerprints.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Just focus on your studies, alright? Make something of yourself. Your mom and I work ourselves to the bone so you don't end up like us.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: We can't give you much. You know that. But we'll give you everything we've got. All you have to do is study hard. That's all we ask.

options: Studying is so exhausting. I give up.
You're right. I want a better life than this.

choices.text: Studying is so exhausting. I give up.
You're right. I want a better life than this.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Pathetic! Seriously, what else are you going to do at your age if not study? Your parents are running themselves into the ground for you, and you're just going to quit? Pick again!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: There we go! Now that's more like it. Your parents are giving you everything they've got. The absolute least you can do is work hard!
The day the acceptance letter arrives from Eastside's best university, her mother cries on the yellowed sofa while her father drinks himself blind, nearly tumbling beside the coffee table.
In this ordinary family, everyone is lit up with genuine joy. The girl stands in her cramped room, facing a wall of certificates curled at the edges, her heart pounding with heat.

She is proud. She is full of fire.
She believes in the world. She believes the rules are fair, that opportunity treats every competitor the same.

So what if she comes from nothing?
Even the most ordinary kid in Eastside, if she works hard enough, will get exactly what she deserves.
She stands at the entrance of the imposing university, gazing up at the old stone halls and the crowds of brilliant young people drawn from across the globe. Not a flicker of doubt crosses her mind.
Her future is bright. She can almost touch it.
[Chapter Two: A Twist of Fate]

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: ...Thankfully, your father's life is no longer in danger. But I need you to prepare yourself. The damage from the accident is permanent. He won't ever fully recover.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Poor thing... Her mother collapsed right while I was changing her father's IV. First the accident, and now this. And she's only just started university. I don't know how she's going to manage all this on her own...
Two thin medical files are all it takes to hold one ordinary family now nearly broken in half. The girl leans against the white wall outside the inpatient ward, tears spilling silently down her face.
But this is a hospital. The one place in the world where tears mean nothing. No one stops. No one looks.
Brrriiing—

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Hello...?

steps.speaker: Fixer
steps.content: Hey, you know that student loan thing you were asking about? I found something. It's a joint program between the school and an outside group, fast-tracked for top students like you. The paperwork's straightforward, and the money comes through quick. Just take it for now. We'll figure out the rest later, alright?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh, sure, don't sign it. Great plan. Forget tuition, you don't even know where dinner's coming from tonight.

The girl never shakes her unease about the loan. In the end, she cannot bring herself to sign.

Not long after, she submits her withdrawal and returns to the cramped house on the city's edge.

She finds a job nearby. By some bitter coincidence, it is the same convenience store where her mother once worked.

She takes hold of the scanner her mother gripped through endless day and night shifts, and when the door chime rings, she looks out past the storefront.

The future she dreamed of as a child is gone. She cannot see it anymore.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: "I can always make more money." Oh, sure, that's the line, isn't it? And it's true! You CAN make more money, but it also goes out. And out. And out.
The loan lands in her account and douses the immediate fire. It also lights the fuse on a nightmare.
With every passing minute, the interest multiplies, feeding on itself like a parasite.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Yes, yes, I understand. I'll have this month's payment ready, I promise...

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I'm sorry. Please, just two more days. My part-time job pays weekly. Just a little more time, please...
The same desperate pleas echo through her small terminal, almost every single day.
She can't bring herself to tell her parents, terrified of adding even more weight to a family already crushed by hardship. So she weeps alone in the dark, swallowing every bitter drop in silence.
[Background Flash]
[Background Flash]
[Background Flash]

From coffee shops to fast food counters, convenience stores to street corners where she hands out flyers, and tutoring sessions after school each day, she works relentlessly. Some days she bounces between four different places, sleeping less than four hours. All for when the month ends, she can receive one fewer call, speak one fewer word of pleading.
Her slipping grades tell the story plainly, yet she dares not stop. If she does, those figures will become a monster and consume her entirely.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: I looked over your last coursework. It's sloppy. You barely put anything into it.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: And you've been distracted in class lately. Completely somewhere else. What's going on? Are you in some kind of trouble?
Maybe it's because he's the first one in recent memory to ask her, "What's going on?" The girl suddenly cannot hold back her tears and bursts into violent sobs.

Everything comes spilling out. The pressure she has been carrying, heavy as a boulder on her chest, finally lifts as the words rush forth. She grips the professor's sleeve the way a drowning person seizes a floating straw.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: ...Poor child. Something this serious, why didn't you come to me sooner?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I... I've let you down... I'm so sorry...

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: Come work in my lab. It won't be easy work, but the pay will be enough. Enough to let you drop a few of those other jobs, get some rest, and put your mind back where it belongs. You still want to study. I can see that.
The professor hands her a clean tissue so she can dry her tears.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You have a real gift for this. Given half a chance, you'll get through this and go far. I believe that.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: So, what do you say?

options: Decline the offer and stick to the part-time arrangement
Gratefully accept the offer and resolve to make the professor proud

choices.text: Decline the offer and stick to the part-time arrangement
Gratefully accept the offer and resolve to make the professor proud

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: An idealist. Hehehe. This isn't some feel-good web novel. You don't claw your way out of the gutter all by yourself. That's not how the real world works.

The girl knows by now that she must not be a burden to others.

A single lab position, after all, will never match the money she can scrape together from juggling multiple jobs out in the city.

She declines the professor's kindness and hurls herself back into work with reckless intensity. Her grades fall off a cliff.

At last, she cannot clear her student loans. What arrives instead is a withdrawal notice and a thin slip of paper with a diagnosis.

The night is cold, as it always is. She stands on the rooftop, watching a city full of lit windows, and sees no light that belongs to her...

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: ...Yes, there we go. How could you not repay him? Without that man, your <color=#fb9259>future</color> wouldn't even exist.
[Chapter Three: The Boiling Frog]

Life in the lab begins unremarkably enough. She organizes data, cleans glassware, and assists the senior students in recording their experiments... Everyone is kind to her, genuinely happy to include her. For the first time, she feels like part of a real team, working together toward something.

The professor never holds back his generosity. Aware of her struggles, he places his meal card in her pocket and simply leaves it there. Occasionally, he takes the entire lab out for a proper meal, urging them to pursue their studies with dedication and build a future they can be proud of.
What she earns is now enough to meet her monthly payments. With the professor's support, she no longer bounces between jobs on an empty stomach, never knowing where her next meal will come from.
Slowly, the harrying phone calls grow fewer and farther between. At last, the girl can catch her breath. She sleeps deeply, opens her textbooks, and lets herself sink into the world of knowledge.
Until one day.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: This dataset here needs a little adjustment.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Adjustment?

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: It's minor. Won't change the overall conclusions at all. But if we submit the numbers as they are, the whole team has to redo the experiment. That's a lot of time down the drain for everyone.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: ...Okay. I'll take care of it.
Then the next time comes.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: This chart needs some polishing. The review board expects cleaner-looking results than this.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: ...I understand.
She is bent over her work, nervously making revisions, when the senior at the next station leans in. After a glance at the screen, she drops a casual comment:

steps.speaker: Older Student
steps.content: Oh, that? Totally standard. Mine went through five rounds of revisions last month. Data, charts, conclusions, all of it. Still got published. Nobody reads that carefully, trust me.
She says it with the offhand ease of someone talking about today's lunch menu.
After that, it's another senior student. One day, while she is organizing her experiment notes, he appears at her side and speaks in a hushed tone.

steps.speaker: Senior
steps.content: Hey. You're strapped for cash, right?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: ...I'm managing.

steps.speaker: Senior
steps.content: Come on. You don't have to pretend. We all know the deal. Look, I've got something. Ghostwriting an undergrad thesis. Not a long one, and the research topic's pretty close to what you're already working on. The pay's enough to cover your expenses for three months. You want in?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: But... isn't that...

steps.speaker: Senior
steps.content: Oh, please. It's nothing. The kid's family has money, but he's got rocks for brains. He's never graduating without help. You help him, he pays you. Everybody's happy. And honestly? We're not the only ones running this kind of thing. Everyone does it.

The words "academic misconduct" rise to her lips, but he's already strolling off with a smile. He tosses back a casual "let me know when you've thought it over," his back radiating total confidence that she'll agree.
Then comes the fourth time, the fifth, the sixth... Each time a "small problem," each one wrapped in a perfectly sensible reason.

Ghostwriting assignments and papers, falsifying lab records, helping spoiled rich kids coast their way to a degree. The seniors treated it all as a "side hustle," eagerly sending clients her way, calling it "resource sharing" and "mutual support."
As time passes by, the girl comes to realize that behind every polished result in this gleaming laboratory, there are secrets that must never be spoken.
But when she looks around, every student wears the same unmoved expression. As if all of this is not only perfectly reasonable to them, but simply how things are done.

options: Follow your conscience and leave the lab
Blend in and become a true part of the lab

choices.text: Follow your conscience and leave the lab
Blend in and become a true part of the lab

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: A conscience! How adorable. I love people with consciences! But here's the thing: conscience doesn't pay the bills. It doesn't put food on the table. So tell me, is it really worth it?

The girl knows it is wrong.

Today, it's falsifying data. Tomorrow, taking credit for someone else's paper. And the day after that?

She can't go on like this. Her student loan has already worn her spirit thin. If she steps onto this dark path as well, where will it lead?

She submits her resignation to the professor and signs a nondisclosure agreement, swearing never to reveal what happens inside that lab.

But the moment she steps outside, she sees the truth. The world has already changed.
She is right back in that hell where the numbers multiply endlessly and swallow her life whole.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Not a bad choice at all. Of course, that all depends on one tiny little thing: whether they actually see you as one of them.
Yes, the professor and the seniors have all been so kind to me. I must repay that kindness. And I need the money to survive. In the end, that reasoning wins out, and the girl makes up her mind.

steps.speaker: K.K.
steps.content: It's just a few small adjustments. It's nothing. I was overthinking it. I don't know any better yet, that's why I got so worried. The professor has his reasons. Everyone has their reasons. This is just... how academia works.
She packs her conscience into a box, seals it tight with tape, and stows it away in a hidden corner of her heart. She tells herself she can open it later, after graduation, once the loan is paid off.
The water is just the right temperature. The frog inside has no desire to jump out. Not yet.
[Chapter Four: His "Gratitude"]

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: This paper is brilliant. I'm very glad I brought you onto this project.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Thank you... There's still a small gap in the data, though. Just give me two more weeks. Two weeks, and I can finish it. Please, give me some more time!

The girl steps out of the office, dark circles heavy beneath her eyes from sleepless nights. But she is happy. She knows that once she fills in the missing data, this paper will be her stepping stone to academia, an achievement she can truly be proud of.
Then, a week later, she sees her paper in a leading journal.
The data is immaculate. Her name appears in a forgotten corner of the page, denied even the status of corresponding author.
She rushes to the professor's office without a second thought.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Professor! You...
Contrary to all her expectations, he does nothing more than lift his eyes to her face.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: It's just a simple exchange of interests. Is there a problem?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: ...An exchange of interests?

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: That authorship has already gotten you money, strong grades, and the chance to keep studying here. You're young. Don't get greedy.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: But that's fraud! I told you, I just needed two more weeks for the data. I could have finished it. I could have made it right. How could you just...

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You want to call it fraud now? Tell me something. Were you really blind to all those "little problems" before?

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You've been looking the other way this whole time, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: The only reason you're standing in my office right now is that this time, the "little problem" finally cost you something. Isn't that the truth?
She tries to speak, but her voice fails her.
She can't remember walking out of that office. All she recalls is the hallway, impossibly long, and the way she had to drag every ounce of herself just to get through it.
The professor's final words stay with her, ringing louder than any of those harrowing phone calls:

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You really don't know how this works? Everyone does it. No one has their hands clean. Do you honestly think every paper in the top journals holds up if you look too close? Do you think those esteemed, distinguished scholars you look up to have never done worse?

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: Welcome to the real world, kid.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: If you're still set on reporting me, go right ahead. But understand something: you had a hand in that falsified data. We've been in the same boat for a long time now.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: I go down, your graduation goes with me. I stay safe, you stay safe.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content:
A win-win. That's the smart choice, isn't it?
And you've always been a smart girl. I know talent when I see it.

options: Refuse to accept this and report him
Agree with him and let it go

choices.text: Refuse to accept this and report him
Agree with him and let it go

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Told you so. Blow the whistle and you go down right alongside him. And look! Here comes your payback, right on schedule!

The girl compiles all the evidence she has and hands it over to the authorities.

On the day she is taken away, she sits in the police car with her hands concealed beneath her jacket, the sound of the handcuffs rattling her senses.

Then one day, inside the detention center, she hears the news update on the television about the academic fraud investigation:

"Investigation concludes Professor B is innocent of all charges. A student maliciously fabricated claims of academic misconduct as an act of revenge..."

In that moment, the world spins and sends her straight into hell.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: The boiling frog should be dead by now.

She goes back to the lab and resumes the work that fills her with disgust.
Day by day, she becomes as numb and mechanical as the instruments around her.

A slow hatred takes root. She hates the data sheets and beakers in her hands. She hates the professor, the seniors, the spoiled rich kids who buy their way through school with purchased papers and fabricated assignments. She hates the corruption of academia. And she hates her own powerlessness even more.
The studies she once loved, and the work she had hoped would speak for her, now nauseate her at a single glance.

What is it she truly needs? A graduation certificate? But if every achievement behind it is fabricated, what does that certificate even mean? A costly testament to her sins, a mark she will carry forever, reminding her that her life is forever tainted?
Sleep abandons her. She lies awake night after night, watching forged data and manipulated charts float past her mind's eye.
Occasionally, she jolts upright, then sinks back down in defeat.
What difference would it make now?
[Chapter Five: The End of Everything]
Then one day, police cars roll onto campus. The lab doors are sealed with tape, and the professor is led away.

She stands among the onlookers, watching, a dark joy stirring inside her.
Just as she had believed when she was young, justice would find its way.
Yet the trial never comes to pass. Instead, she is called into an office and made to sit before a panel of investigators.

steps.speaker: Investigator
steps.content: You were the professor's assistant, yes? You processed the data. Your name is on that paper. We've spoken with your fellow students, and they've confirmed your involvement.

steps.speaker: Investigator
steps.content: Is there anything you'd like to add?

Anything she'd like to add? Of course she has something to say. She has plenty to say. But when she seeks out witnesses to stand beside her, each one lowers their gaze and retreats into the shadows like a rat vanishing into its hole, refusing to utter a single word.

steps.speaker: Classmate
steps.content: Sorry, I was just helping out here and there. Whatever was going on between you and the professor, I wouldn't know anything about that.

steps.speaker: Roommate A
steps.content: Sorry. I got into grad school. I have to move out basically right now. The program's starting early. Let's catch up another time.

steps.speaker: Roommate B (Phone)
steps.content: "Beep... Beep... The number you have dialed is currently unavailable. Please..."

She ends the call, and the phone slides from her fingers. Beyond the window, graduating students stroll under the shade of the trees, their laughter bright, their eyes fixed on the future. She remains in the gloom of her dormitory, the door closed on her from the outside, abandoned to her own helplessness.
In the end, everyone else gets what they wanted.
It turns out she is the one they can throw away at any time.
An official reprimand. Withdrawal procedures. Her name placed on the academic blacklist and on the permanent exclusion rosters of every university that matters.
The whole machinery grinds through in under three days, swift as though the outcome had been decided long before. She is shoved along every step of the way, powerless to resist.
One last time, she sits down at her computer and logs into the campus system.

She only finds her student ID revoked, her inbox and the academic database no longer accessible.
All those sleepless nights spent compiling data. Every sentence she carefully typed. The works she poured her heart into that were eventually published under another's name...
University Website Notice [You don't have permission to access this resource.]
She stares at those words, then opens her personal folder to find rows of files turned gray.
The cursor pulses on the screen like a sneer, ridiculing her for ever daring to reach so high.
She begins copying the file names into a memo, one after another, as if this small act might leave some trace of her behind. But midway, her fingers fall still.
What's the point?
These things were never hers, not from the very start.

A pressure builds in her chest, hot and burning, threatening to tear her apart from the inside. Her hands shake above the keys. Then she does what the girl she once was would never have had the courage to do.

options: Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!

choices.text: Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!

steps.content: She grabs the keyboard and slams it into the screen.

The thunderous impact cracks through both, sending shards scattering in every direction. Then she grabs the monitor and throws it to the ground, picks up the chair, and swings. Once. Twice. Three times.
Her mind is empty through it all, save for one circling thought: she is already expelled, already has nothing, already free from ever having to be the good student again.
Out in the corridor, someone glances through the half-open door and stares with a mixture of shock and disdain. The old her would have been crushed by that look. Now, she only thinks it is absurd.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: The hell are you looking at? What, never seen a crazy person before?

After she has destroyed everything within reach, she stands panting amid the ruins and realizes her hand is bleeding. Perhaps the glass got her, or a flying shard of plastic. She looks down at it for a moment, then raises that bloodied hand and flips off what remains of the computer.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Don't have permission? **** you!

Her reflection stares back from the broken monitor, split into jagged fragments. She looks at those scattered pieces of herself for a long moment, then breaks into laughter.
A sense of relief washes over her, pure and unlike anything she has ever known.

On the day she carries her luggage out through the school gates, the weather is impossibly fine. Sunlight drapes itself over the magnificent entrance, the ancient buildings, the students strolling past with futures shining in their eyes.
Inside the library, heads are bent over books. The labs glow with relentless light. Everything remains so orderly, so lovely, so full of promise.

And she, standing beyond the iron gates, takes it all in and begins to laugh. A small sound at first, then swelling until it racks her body. She bends at the waist, tears spilling down her cheeks, unable to separate the laughter from the weeping.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Fairness. Justice.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Hard work changes your fate.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: A ladder to climb. A sanctuary of knowledge.
What pretty words they are. Each one glitters. Each one fills people with longing.
But what is the truth?

The truth is that rules, power, and interest are interlocked, fitted together like a perfectly engineered machine. Those seated high above are the operators. Ordinary people are nothing but parts. A part wears out, it gets replaced. It outlives its use, it gets discarded.

They spin those beautiful lies and illusions so people believe that effort will be rewarded, that everyone has equal opportunities. All so people will stay a dutiful little part, squeezed dry, used up, and cast aside.
When the laughter fades at last, she straightens her back and glances over her shoulder at the campus one final time. At that instant, something detonates deep within her.
She majored in biochemistry. She knows perfectly well what Sinners and their awakened powers are.

And then it hits her. That power might be the only crack in this seamless system, the one opening an ordinary person can pry apart. It is the thing those above cannot fully command, the final chance bestowed by fate upon a scapegoat.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: If being the good little rule-follower gets you nothing...
She tightens her fist, and blood begins to seep between her fingers. Her face no longer carries fear, nor hesitation, nor the torment of wondering whether what she does is right.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Then fine. A lunatic it is.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Everything you took from me, I'm taking back. This whole machine that ate me alive, along with countless others like me... I'm going to tear it apart until there's nothing left!
